$description: The approved Mentora course-artwork system — extracted from the locked showcase's § 12 'Course artwork — one family, five recognisable subjects' and cross-referenced against the current web implementation's CourseThumbnail component (implementation EVIDENCE that this system is correctly implemented, per SOURCE_MANIFEST.json rank 4 — not itself a design source). Governs every place a course thumbnail renders: CourseCard, CourseProgressCard, Course Details hero, Checkout line item, Learning Path Details course-list rows.

governanceNote.quote: these bases and motifs are an artwork system, not application UI colours — they must never enter the semantic colour tokens
governanceNote.implication: The 5 gradient bases and their motif icons below are correctly implemented as literal CSS/values in the artwork component, NOT as new design-tokens.json entries. This is the one place in the product where a literal value is governed-and-approved rather than a DESIGN_RULES.md rule-18 violation — the exception is explicit and narrow, scoped to this system only.

aspectRatio: 16:9 — same convention as CourseCard thumbnail and VideoPlayer, so artwork scales from an 88px list thumbnail to a full-width hero without re-composition (source: showcase § 12, exact quote: "artwork scales from an 88px list thumbnail to a full-width hero without re-composition").

compositionRecipe.$description: Every course-artwork rendering is composed of exactly these four layers, in this order.
layers: 1. Base — a dark purple/indigo gradient, one of 5 (see motifSystem below), selected deterministically from the course's category/seed so the SAME course always renders the SAME artwork.
2. Motif — one geometric icon/pattern that names the subject (e.g. bar-chart glyph for Data & Analytics), centered or off-center per the showcase composition.
3. Light source — a soft directional highlight/gradient overlay for depth, not a flat fill.
4. Category chip — overlaid on the artwork's own scrim (color.overlay.chipScrim), pinned to the logical-start corner, NOT placed below the thumbnail in the card body.

motifSystem.$description: 5 category-motif pairs, deterministically assigned per category (or per course as a fallback when no category-level assignment exists) — never random per render, so the same course always shows the same artwork. The gradient CSS below is copied verbatim from the current, working implementation (web/src/components/ui/course-thumbnail.tsx's ARTWORK_MOTIFS, D48) — implementation EVIDENCE (SOURCE_MANIFEST.json rank 4) that this is how the showcase's 'dark purple/indigo base' rule (rank 3) was correctly realized as a literal, governed value (design-system/DESIGN_RULES.md rule 18 exception, see governanceNote above). This is now the SOURCE the web generator reads to produce ARTWORK_MOTIFS — course-thumbnail.tsx no longer hand-defines this array (see design-to-code/validation/MAPPING_REPORT.md).

motifs.gradient: radial-gradient(circle at 84% 16%, rgba(255,255,255,0.22), transparent 48%), repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 6%, rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 6% 10%), linear-gradient(135deg, #241C5C 0%, #4A3EB0 58%, #4A62F0 100%)

repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.14) 0 1px, transparent 1px 9%), radial-gradient(circle at 76% 78%, rgba(255,255,255,0.20), transparent 42%), linear-gradient(135deg, #35257F 0%, #6558D3 60%, #7C4DFF 100%)

repeating-radial-gradient(circle at 72% 50%, rgba(255,255,255,0.16) 0 1.5px, transparent 1.5px 13px), radial-gradient(circle at 72% 50%, rgba(255,255,255,0.22), transparent 30%), linear-gradient(135deg, #1C2470 0%, #3B4278 50%, #4A62F0 100%)

radial-gradient(circle at 20% 20%, rgba(255,255,255,0.20), transparent 46%), repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.13) 0 1px, transparent 1px 18%), repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.13) 0 1px, transparent 1px 14%), linear-gradient(135deg, #3B2A7A 0%, #6558D3 55%, #7C4DFF 100%)

motifSystem.assignmentRule: seed = course.categoryId (preferred) falling back to a stable hash of course.courseId if no category mapping exists — never a random per-render pick, so a given course's card looks identical everywhere it appears in the app. Hash function: hash = (hash*31 + charCode) >>> 0 over the seed string, motif index = hash % 5.

categoryChipOverlay.position: logical-start corner of the artwork, overlaid ON the artwork's own scrim — NOT below the thumbnail in the card body.
categoryChipOverlay.background: color.overlay.chipScrim (rgba(17,18,23,0.72) in both themes — deliberately theme-invariant, same rationale as VideoPlayer's control bar)
categoryChipOverlay.distinctFrom: color.overlay.scrim (rgba(17,18,23,0.48) light / rgba(0,0,0,0.64) dark) — chipScrim is a separate, higher-contrast, theme-invariant token specifically for a legible chip on top of arbitrary artwork colors.

fallbackBehavior.$description: What happens when a real course thumbnail asset is broken, missing, or (in seed/demo data) literal undecodable placeholder bytes — the artwork system itself IS the fallback, not a secondary fallback behind it.
fallbackBehavior.detection: onError + onLoad (checking naturalWidth === 0) + a requestAnimationFrame check after mount for the already-cached case — a broken image can return a normal 200/image content-type with naturalWidth 0, which never fires a plain onError.
fallbackBehavior.rendering: the deterministic motif/gradient artwork renders in place of the broken image — there is no secondary flat-color or icon-only fallback, because the artwork system is content-neutral by design (it never depended on a real photo to look intentional).

constraintsPreventingGenericSameness.$description: What stops every course from reading as 'the same generic purple rectangle,' per the mission's explicit concern.
rules: 5 distinct motif/icon pairs, not 1 — a course's category visibly changes its artwork's iconography, not just its category-chip label.
Deterministic per-course/per-category assignment means a user browsing Explore sees visual variety across the grid, not repetition of a single gradient.

The category chip overlay itself is a second, independent signal (text + icon-implied category) reinforcing the motif — content resilience holds even if a user can't distinguish two similar gradients at a glance.

Gradient direction/light-source treatment gives each card a sense of depth distinct from a truly flat single-color rectangle, per the showcase's explicit 'not a generic purple rectangle' composition intent.

realCourseArtwork.$description: Course-Artwork-Identity ticket: the fallback motif/gradient system above is deterministically assigned per CATEGORY (assignmentRule: 'seed = course.categoryId preferred'). Seed data has 4 real published courses across only 3 categories — 'Building Reliable REST APIs' and 'Kotlin Coroutines in Practice' both carry category 'Software Development' (SeedData.kt COURSES), so both rendered the identical 'code' motif/gradient everywhere CourseThumbnail renders them, reading as generic/repeated artwork rather than distinct per-course identity. Real per-course artwork resolves this without touching the fallback system, the CourseThumbnail component, or any consuming screen: CourseThumbnail already renders a real `mediaId` image ahead of the motif fallback (see fallbackBehavior above — 'the artwork system itself IS the fallback'), so this is the system behaving exactly as designed once real images exist.
realCourseArtwork.mechanism: backend/src/main/kotlin/com/mentora/backend/SeedData.kt's ensureCourseArtwork seed step uploads one real, topic-specific JPEG per targeted course through the existing MediaService `courseThumbnail` pipeline (same upload path/endpoint as an instructor-authored thumbnail) and sets it as `thumbnailMediaId` on the course — no new endpoint, schema field, or React code. Every screen already reads `course.thumbnailMediaId` into CourseThumbnail's `mediaId` prop, so the same image renders consistently everywhere: Landing, Explore, Dashboard, My Learning, Course Details, Course Player, Checkout, Learning Path Details.
realCourseArtwork.visualDesign: Each image keeps the exact governed composition recipe (dark purple/indigo/violet gradient base + soft directional light-source highlight + one centered white geometric icon, 16:9, no embedded text) so it reads as the same Mentora artwork family as the motif fallback, not a different visual system — only the gradient balance and icon differ per course, staying inside the existing color palette (#1C2470-#4A62F0 range) rather than inventing an off-brand one.

courses.subject: API/network topology — a hub node with radiating endpoint connections

courses.courseTitle: أساسيات تصميم تجربة المستخدم (User Experience Design Fundamentals)
courses.subject: a UI wireframe/mockup screen

realCourseArtwork.contentTruthfulness: Purely visual (gradient + icon), no embedded text in any language, so it carries no content-language claim — the course-content-truthfulness rule (a course's real lesson/video content must stay in its true contentLanguage regardless of a translated display title, see the Course Localized Metadata ticket) is unaffected and does not need to extend to artwork.
realCourseArtwork.scopeNote: Every other seeded course (both drafts, and any future course without an entry above) continues to render the governed 5-motif fallback unchanged — this section only documents the 4 real, published courses this ticket targets, per its explicit 'do not invent unrelated UI features' scope.
realCourseArtwork.crossPlatform: Because the mechanism is a served media URL (`/api/v1/media/{id}/file`) rather than web-only CSS, Android/iOS inherit the identical artwork identity for free by pointing an image view at the same course's `thumbnailMediaId` — no gradient/pattern reimplementation needed on those platforms.
